0. FOREWORD

0.1 This lndian Standard (Second Revision 1 was adopted by the Indian Standards lnstitution on 29 September 1983, after the draft finalized by the Hair Cutting, Shaving, Shearing and Allied Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1956 and revised in 1965. The present revision has been taken up to incorporate certain additional sizes of razors which are in vogue. The values of length of blade and length of handle have been modified. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4.1 The blades shall be forg:d. The handle scales shall be properly shaped and finished smooth and free from sharp edges. The blades shall be securely and neatly fitted to the handle scales by rivets. The blades shall be well and evenly hardened and tempered and shall then be made hollow-ground in a direction at right angles to the cutting edge. The tang shall be properly serrated as shown in the figure. The packing piece shall be fitted between the scales at the free end by rivets.
NOTE--Manufacturers are recommended to subject the steel forgings to spheroidizing treatment. This facilitates uniform hardness which is essential for quality razors, and gives them a keen and straight edge on repeated re-sharpening. 5.

HARDNESS The testing

5.1 The blade shall have a hardness of 700 to 800 HP. point shall be as near as practicable to the cutting edge. 6. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH

6.1 The blade shall be free from seams, pits, burrs, laminations, cracks and other imperfections. Except for the serrated portion and cutting edge, it shall be finished smooth and shall be polished bright all over. The serrations shall be well formed. The rivet head shall be well shaped. The blade shall work freely without any undue play or stiffness. Grinding marks shall not be visible on the blade particularly near the cutting edge, when examined under a microscope at a magnification of 15 X. 6.2 The cutting edge shall be free from waviness and undulations examined under a microscope at a magnification of 60 X:
a) at

when

right angles to the blade surface, and

b) parallel to the blade edge. 6.3 The bIade shall be sharpened 6.4 When closed, handle. 7. DESIGNATION

8. SAMPLING 8.1 The number of razors to be selected from a lot for ascertaining conformity to this specification shall be as agreed to between A suitable sampling scheme and the manufacturer and the purchaser. criteria for conformity for razors is given in Appendix A. 9. TEST 9.1 Rust-Proofness - The surface of the blade shall be cleaned by When dry, the razor some suitable solvent to remove greasy matter. shall be stored in a damp box, the relative humidity of which shall be maintained at 95 percent for six days. Gn removal from the damp box, the razor blade shall not show any sign for rusting. 9.2 Plastics,Handles 9.2.1 Boiling - The razor shall be immersed completely for 1 hour in a boiling 5 percent soap solution, then rinsed immediately in water at 15 to 20�C and immediately re-immersed completely in boiling water for 1 hour. The razors shall then be rinsed again in water at 15 to 20�C. This procedure shall be repeated four times. During or on completion of the test, the handle shall not show any sign of cracking, chipping or discolouring of the plastics. The tang shall neither become loose nor shall there be any other damage. 9.2.2 Impact - This test shall be conducted after the boiling test. The razor in closed position shall be held vertically with the pivot end upwards and dropped from a height of 1'2 m on to a concrete floor or on a flat stone five rimes in succession. The height shall be measured from the lowest point of the razor. To avoid the blade coming out of the scales, the razor shall be tied with a string as near to be pivot During or on completion of the test, the as possible before dropping. handle shall not show any sign of cracking, breaking or chipping of the plastics and tang shall neither become loose nor shall there be any other damages after the test. 6

IS:88810. MARKING

1983

10.1 Each razor shall be legibly and indelibly stamped on the tang of the blade with nominal size, manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade-mark. When specifically required by the purchaser, the year of manufacture shall also be marked. 10.1.1

The

razors

may also be stamped-with

the ISI Certification

Mark.
NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply uith the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspec:ion. testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

11. PRESERVATIVE

TREATMENT

AND PACKING

11.1 The blade shall be coated with a suitable rust preventive.

11.2 Each razor shall be wrapped in glassine paper and placed in clothbound cardboard carton or in a strong cardboard carton. 11.3 The cartons shall be labelled on one side indicating the size, manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark. Five or ten such cartons shall again be packed in a cardboard box labelled on the side indicating the description of the contents and the manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark.

A-2. NUMBER OF TEST AND CRITERIA

FOR CONFORMITY

A-2.1 The razors selected according to A-l.2 shall be tested for (a) dimensions ( see 2.1 ), (b) hardness ( see 5.1 ), (c) workmanship and finish ( see 6 ), and (d) tests for plastics handles ( see 9.2 ). A-2.2 The number of razors to be tested for the resistance to rusting ( see 9.1 ) shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 4 of Table 1. These razors may be selected from the razors already tested under A-2.1 and found satisfactory. A-2.3 Criteria for Conformity-The lot shall be declared conforming to the requirements of this standard if the conditions given in A-2.3.1 and A-2.3.2 are satisfied. A-2.3.1 The number of razors found defective for one or more characteristics mentioned in A-2.1 is less than or equal to corresponding acceptance number given in co1 3 of Table 1.
